rationale: Reviewed spec.md and ADR-0045 at 7a4900643c5b567d6074070264ce166c57209f74, with the G3 adversarial lens on R4 and R6. The panel-set design retains the important safeguards in its stated requirements: a real reachable two-parent subject-nominated candidate, exact second-parent equality, binding/branch contradiction vetoes, and revert discrimination. I did not find a new panel-registration-only forgery bypass in those stated rules. However, R4.1 names a membership resolver that cannot implement the specified membership contract, creating an unsafe exemption path for closed metadata-only dependencies. R6 also promotes existing advisory markers into reusable claim authorization without defining evidence validation or legacy-marker treatment, and its ACs do not adequately pin scope across persistence and explicit narrower requests. Six scratch-only baseline probes passed; results are in probe-results.txt and probe sources are in repo/internal/{phase,lifecycle,next}/g3_probe_test.go. These establish current behavior, not a test of the unimplemented proposal. The reviewed repository was not modified. GitHub issue reads for 239, 232 and 255 failed because api.github.com was unreachable, so no independent issue-content conclusions are claimed.
concrete_changes_required: Revise R4.1 and AC-9 to define status-independent, tracker-fact membership for CLOSED dependencies: descendant of the spec epic OR matching metadata.spec_id, without using the bd-ready result set or title fallback. Price the necessary resolver/read changes in scope. Distinguish confirmed non-membership from lookup/parse failures so failures cannot earn the closed-only exemption. Add fixtures for a closed metadata-only same-spec bead with no parent or title hint and no merge (FAIL), a title-only non-member, and an indeterminate membership read (fail closed). Reconcile the same resolver gap with AC-1's metadata-only member claim path, which currently reaches EvaluateReadiness's lineage lookup before claim.

Define a shared validity contract for override-marker read-back in ready-check and GateReadiness, including supported signal IDs and evidence schema/integrity checks, and explicitly disposition existing signals-plus-timestamp markers that have no evidence. Missing or malformed evidence must not silently acquire the new evidence-backed authorization guarantee. Require fresh scoped evidence for such markers, or explicitly document and test a visibly distinguished compatibility policy. Add negative read-back and reclaim fixtures for legacy/malformed markers; this does not require cryptographic authentication of agent-writable metadata.

Extend AC-14 through AC-16 with a persistence-based scope-widening regression: request MF-2,MF-3 while only MF-3 fails, assert the stored marker contains only MF-3, then make MF-2 fail and require both ready-check and an unflagged reclaim to refuse. Also pin precedence when an existing marker covers MF-2,MF-3 but a new explicit request names only MF-3 while both fail: R6.1's other-signal refusal must not be bypassed by silently unioning in the old marker. Invalid signal IDs must refuse before mutation.

findings.title: R4.1's existing lineage resolver cannot safely classify the new membership union
findings.detail: spec.md:113 requires same-spec membership per R1.1 while resolving through existing findEpicForBeadFn lineage, never titles. The actual phase.FindEpicForBeadWithCache reads Title and Dependencies, ignores metadata.spec_id, and explicitly falls back to parsing the title. Scratch probe TestG3MetadataOnlyClosedMemberHasNoLineage returns ErrNoEpicLineage for a closed bead linked only by metadata.spec_id=S; TestG3TitleOnlyNonMemberResolvesLineage resolves a parentless, metadata-less '[129]' title to S. Treating the former no-lineage result as the plain-task exemption lets a same-spec closed-but-unmerged dependency PASS MF-3. Propagating it instead leaves the promised metadata-only membership unsupported. R1.1's actual SpecMembers working API is also ready-set based, so it cannot simply classify closed dependencies. AC-9's generic same-spec fixture does not pin this boundary. EvaluateReadiness also uses the same lineage resolver for the selected bead itself, so AC-1's metadata-only claim needs this issue resolved end to end.

findings.title: R6 reuses evidence-less and malformed markers without a validity policy
findings.detail: spec.md:127 requires file evidence for scoped overrides, but :128 and AC-16 authorize any recorded failing signals on later ready-check/reclaim without specifying what constitutes a valid marker. TestG3ExistingOverrideMarkerHasNoEvidence confirms the current writer produces only signals and overridden; these are real upgrade inputs, not hypothetical malformed fixtures. A legacy marker with signals=[MF-3] therefore satisfies the written subset rule even though its evidence fields do not exist. Likewise no read-side behavior is specified for missing evidence, inconsistent bytes/digest/text, unknown IDs, or invalid timestamps. AC-15 verifies the writer only. The new reader must have an explicit compatibility and validation contract so recorded bits do not silently stand in for the evidence-backed bypass this spec promises. Metadata remains forgeable; self-consistency validation is not proof of an operator's identity.

findings.title: Override ACs allow scope to widen after a passing signal is named
findings.detail: R6.1/R6.2 correctly require named-but-passing signals not to be recorded, but AC-14 only checks the note for that case. Its marker assertion uses a request that already names only the failing signal. An implementation can print the correct note while persisting all requested IDs and pass those assertions; when the previously passing signal later fails, AC-16's subset reader then authorizes it without a deliberate override of that failure. AC-16 also does not distinguish implicit reuse from a new explicit narrower request, leaving an implementation room to union the old marker into the new request despite R6.1's requirement to refuse other failures. An end-to-end write/change/read/reclaim fixture should pin both boundaries.

findings.title: Abandoned registrations already corroborate; exact topology and contradiction vetoes remain essential
findings.detail: TestG3AbandonedMatchingPanelAlreadyCorroborates confirms an abandoned registration alone already identifies a real named merge when its SHA equals the second parent and the branch/binding are absent. That is not introduced by R4.3, and MF-3 corroboration is not a successful panel-vote check. TestG3ForgedPanelCannotInventNamedMerge confirms a registration pointing at another bead's actual second parent still cannot create a subject-nominated candidate. TestG3MatchingPanelCannotHideNewUnlandedBranchTip confirms an exact matching panel SHA cannot outvote a surviving branch with newer unlanded work. R4.3 explicitly preserves that veto and binding contradictions; a matching member of the new set must never become an early successful return that skips them. Forging subject-nominated spec history remains outside ADR-0041's documented defended model.

findings.title: Errors in this BRIEF
findings.detail: The generated panel header instructs writing <slot>-round-1.json beside BRIEF, conflicting with the direct task's exact scratch/verdict.json destination and read-only source-repository rule. The conduct section suggests git worktree add against the reviewed repository, which would also mutate its git administrative state despite the read-only instruction. I followed the direct task: cloned under scratch, checked out the reviewed commit there, and wrote only the requested scratch verdict. The leading Summary/Files/Acceptance Criteria/Lens sections retain TODO placeholders before their substantive duplicates; the later sections provide usable review instructions. No additional technical error in the brief was established by this lens.
